podcast.body: This song became a top 40 hit in 1992, marking The Cure as part of an exclusive group of alt-rock bands that achieved commercial success. Its happy tone served as an entry point for many new listeners, who then explored the band's deeper, sadder Goth material, helping bring Goth to the forefront during the alternative 90s. "The Cure, formerly a pure goth band with her top 40 hit from 1992, Friday I'm in love, making them part of that exclusive group of alt rock bands with commercial success."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song highlights Robert Smith's impressive vocal range, showcasing both very high notes, reaching a D6, and very low notes, descending to a D3. This demonstrates his experimentation with different vocal styles throughout his career, from punk to a softer approach, and later an agonized lover persona with yelping falsetto and low growls. "He reaches a very high D, a D6, if you want to get technical in Friday, I'm in love, the same song in which he goes down for a D3."
